symptom: Vacuum pressure rises or specified negative pressure [710 mm Hg (28 in Hg)] cannot be obtained during evacuation
corrective_action: Charge one can [about 0.4 kg (0.9 lb)] of refrigerant into system, check entire system with leak detector, repair leaks, and repeat evacuation to 710 mm Hg (28 in Hg)

symptom: Halide leak detector flame turns yellow (propane type) or bright blue (butane type)
corrective_action: Locate exact leak point, tighten connection fittings using two wrenches, or replace damaged seals/lines

symptom: Halide leak detector flame turns purple (propane type) or vivid green (butane type)
corrective_action: Ventilate area immediately; locate leak point and replace defective component, gasket, O-ring, or hose assembly

symptom: Almost no refrigerant / Continuous bubbles in sight glass
corrective_action: Stop compressor and conduct overall leak check, repair as required, evacuate and recharge system.

symptom: Insufficient refrigerant / Bubbles at 1-2 second intervals
corrective_action: Check for gas leakage, repair as required, replenish and charge system.

symptom: Too much refrigerant / High pressure side abnormally hot
corrective_action: Discharge refrigerant slowly from service valve on low pressure side until proper pressure is reached.

probable_cause: Blown fuse, open ground circuit, faulty blower speed switch, failed blower resistor, open wire, or defective blower motor
corrective_action: Follow blower motor diagnoses tree: test fuse, test ground wires with 12V test light, check resistor and relay, replace defective part.

symptom: Compressor does not run / clutch not engaged
probable_cause: Blown fuse, disconnected clutch lead, faulty micro switch, defective thermostat, or open blower switch contact
corrective_action: Follow compressor clutch diagnoses tree using 12V test lamp to isolate open circuit between ignition, micro switch, thermostat, and clutch coil.

symptom: Compressor clutch engaged but compressor does not run
probable_cause: Low coil voltage (< 10.5V), slipping clutch, loose/worn belt, or seized compressor cylinder
corrective_action: Inspect ground terminal, readjust clutch air gap, clean friction surface, adjust belt tension, or repair/replace compressor.

symptom: Abnormal discharge air temperature but system pressure normal
probable_cause: Air leaks around dash panel grommets, deteriorated body seals, or faulty air flow duct doors
corrective_action: Check grommets on dash panel for air leaks; inspect seals and check air flow duct system.

symptom: Suction pressure is high, while head pressure is low
probable_cause: Compressor internal valve or gasket damaged
Refrigerant overcharge, non-condensable air in system, or clogged/dented condenser fins
corrective_action: Discharge excess refrigerant, or discharge/replace receiver drier/evacuate and recharge, or clean condenser exterior fins with cold water.

probable_cause: Bent evaporator fins/tubes, restricted expansion valve, leaking thermal bulb, restricted pipe strainer, or clogged receiver drier
corrective_action: Straighten evaporator fins, replace expansion valve, clean/replace strainer, or replace receiver drier.

symptom: Moisture in system / Periodic vacuum on suction gauge with needle vibration
probable_cause: Receiver drier saturated with moisture; moisture freezing and plugging orifice in expansion valve
corrective_action: Discharge system, replace receiver drier, perform complete 30-minute evacuation three consecutive times, and recharge.

probable_cause: Restriction or blockage in receiver drier or high pressure pipe strainer
corrective_action: Discharge system, replace receiver drier or strainer, evacuate and recharge.

symptom: Compressor noise only when clutch is engaged
probable_cause: Loose compressor mounting bolts, loose drive belt, or damaged internal compressor parts
corrective_action: Retighten mounting bolts to 4.5-5.5 kg-m, adjust belt deflection to 8-12 mm, or overhaul/replace compressor.

symptom: Compressor noise when clutch is disengaged
probable_cause: Worn or defective compressor clutch pulley bearing
corrective_action: Remove compressor drive belt, spin clutch pulley by hand, and repair or replace compressor clutch pulley assembly.

probable_cause: Contact between pulley and clutch hub.
Loose bracket bolt, cracked or broken bracket.

symptom: Rough rotation (can be sensed by hand) - Roughness
Rough rotation (can be sensed by hand) - Seizure
Rough rotation (can be sensed by hand) - Erratic operation
corrective_action: Check and add oil or replace cylinder assembly.

probable_cause: Gas leaking from magnetic clutch mounting.
corrective_action: Replace shaft seal and shaft seal seat.
Replace discharge valve or rear end cover.

probable_cause: Gas leaking between end cover (R) and shell.
Gas leaking between end cover (F) and shell.

symptom: Test light OFF on yellow wire leading to pressure switch
probable_cause: Wire discontinuity on electric power source of compressor relay, or faulty relay/fuse.
corrective_action: Check wire discontinuity, check relay and fuse, replace relay if necessary.

symptom: Air comes out of heater outlets too in A/C position
probable_cause: Mode door return spring broken, mode door actuator D1 faulty, or vacuum selector valve hose piping faulty.
corrective_action: Check mode door return spring; replace actuator or vacuum selector valve.

symptom: Outside air is being cooled in A/C position
probable_cause: Air intake door return spring broken, air intake door actuator faulty, or vacuum selector valve hose piping faulty.
corrective_action: Check door return spring; replace actuator or vacuum selector valve.

symptom: Air does not come out of air conditioner outlets in A/C position
probable_cause: Mode door return spring broken, mode door actuator D1/D2 faulty, or vacuum selector valve piping faulty.
corrective_action: Check mode door return spring; replace actuator or vacuum selector valve.

probable_cause: FICD actuator faulty, FICD magnet valve faulty, vacuum tank leak, check valve faulty, or damaged hose/connector.
corrective_action: Inspect actuator hose, check magnet valve power, inspect vacuum tank and check valve, repair or replace faulty parts.

symptom: Air comes out of heater outlets too in VENT position
probable_cause: Mode door return spring broken, actuator D1 faulty, or vacuum selector valve hose piping incorrect.
corrective_action: Check return spring, replace actuator or vacuum selector valve.

symptom: Air comes out while outside air does not come in in VENT position
probable_cause: Air intake door actuator faulty, vacuum selector valve faulty, magnet valve faulty, vacuum tank leaking, or check valve faulty.
corrective_action: Check hose connection, replace actuator, vacuum selector valve, magnet valve, or check valve as required.

symptom: Air comes out of heater outlets alone in BI-LEVEL position
probable_cause: Mode door return spring broken, actuator faulty, or vacuum selector valve hose piping incorrect.
corrective_action: Check return spring, replace actuator or vacuum selector valve.

symptom: Air comes out of air conditioner outlets alone in BI-LEVEL position
probable_cause: Mode door actuator D1 faulty, vacuum selector valve faulty, magnet valve, vacuum tank, or check valve faulty.
corrective_action: Check hose connection, replace actuator, vacuum selector valve, magnet valve, or check valve.

symptom: Hot air comes out but outside air is not heated in HEAT position
probable_cause: Air intake door actuator faulty or vacuum selector valve / vacuum source faulty.
corrective_action: Check hose connection, replace actuator or vacuum selector valve.

symptom: Hot air does not come out in HEAT position
probable_cause: Water cock control wire disconnected, or vacuum cock / vacuum source faulty.
corrective_action: Reconnect control wire, replace vacuum cock, vacuum selector valve, or magnet valve.

symptom: Air does not come out at all in HEAT position
probable_cause: Heater door closed (wire faulty) or mode door actuator D1/D2 faulty.
corrective_action: Check control wire and replace heater door wire; check mode door actuator hoses and replace actuator.

symptom: Hot air comes out but inside air is not heated in REC HEAT position
probable_cause: Air intake door return spring broken, actuator faulty, or vacuum selector valve piping incorrect.
corrective_action: Check return spring, replace actuator or vacuum selector valve.

symptom: Hot air does not come out in REC HEAT position
probable_cause: Water cock control wire disconnected or vacuum cock faulty.
corrective_action: Reconnect control wire, check vacuum cock hose connection, replace vacuum cock.

symptom: Air does not come out at all in REC HEAT position
probable_cause: Heater door closed (wire faulty) or mode door actuator D1/D2 faulty.
corrective_action: Check control wire, replace heater door wire or mode door actuator.

symptom: Hot air comes out but outside air is not heated in DEFROST position
probable_cause: Air intake door actuator faulty or vacuum supply problem.
corrective_action: Check hose connection, replace actuator or vacuum source components.

symptom: Hot air does not come out in DEFROST position
probable_cause: Water cock control wire disconnected or vacuum cock faulty.
corrective_action: Reconnect control wire, replace vacuum cock.

symptom: Air does not come out at all in DEFROST position
probable_cause: Mode door does not operate (air comes out of A/C outlets) or blower does not run.
corrective_action: Check mode door actuator hoses, replace actuator, or refer to Blower Motor Diagnoses.

symptom: Air comes out only a little in DEFROST position
probable_cause: Mode door is only half operative (actuator D2 faulty) or heater door is not closed (control wire disconnected).
corrective_action: Connect vacuum tester to hose D2 of double actuator, replace actuator, or reconnect heater door control wire.
Replace drive plate if runout exceeds 0.5 mm (0.020 in)

symptom: Transmission binds or rotates stiffly after torque converter installation
probable_cause: Torque converter notch not engaged properly with oil pump
corrective_action: Check that distance 'A' is more than 21.5 mm (0.846 in) and reinstall converter aligning notches properly

symptom: Torque converter oil fouled or contaminated due to burnt clutch
corrective_action: Flush torque converter thoroughly with non-lead gasoline/kerosene and torque converter oil

symptom: Oil distributor seal ring to ring groove clearance excessive
probable_cause: Worn seal ring or distributor groove
corrective_action: Replace seal ring or oil distributor assembly if clearance is outside 0.04 to 0.16 mm (0.0016 to 0.0063 in)

symptom: Engine does not start in 'N', 'P' ranges.
probable_cause: Faulty ignition switch/starter motor, range select linkage out of adjustment, or defective inhibitor switch and wiring.
corrective_action: Check ignition switch and starter motor (1), range select linkage (2), inhibitor switch and wiring (3).

symptom: Engine starts in other range than 'N' and 'P'.
probable_cause: Range select linkage misadjusted or defective/misadjusted inhibitor switch.
corrective_action: Check range select linkage (1), inhibitor switch and wiring (2).

symptom: Sharp shock in shifting from 'N' to 'D' range.
probable_cause: Excessive engine stall rpm, high engine idling rpm, faulty rear lubrication, or defective rear clutch.
corrective_action: Check engine stall rpm (1), engine idling rpm (2), rear lubrication (3), governor valve (4), rear clutch (5).

symptom: Vehicle will not run in 'D' range (but runs in '2', '1' and 'R' ranges).
probable_cause: Range select linkage out of adjustment, low throttle oil pressure, manual control valve defect, or slipping transmission one-way clutch.
corrective_action: Check range select linkage (1), throttle oil pressure (2), manual control valve (3), one-way clutch of transmission (4).

symptom: Vehicle will not run in 'D', '1', '2' ranges (but runs in 'R' range). Clutch slips. Very poor acceleration.
probable_cause: Low oil level, range select linkage, transmission air check leakage, engine idling rpm, rear lubrication, band servo, ignition/starter, rear clutch slipping, or defective oil pump.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), linkage (2), transmission air check (3), idling rpm (4), rear lubrication (5), band servo (6), ignition (7), rear clutch (8), oil pump (9).

symptom: Vehicle will not run in 'R' range (but runs in 'D', '2' and '1' ranges). Clutch slips. Very poor acceleration.
probable_cause: Oil level, linkage, idling rpm, air check, rear lubrication, band servo, low & reverse brake slipping, front clutch slipping, rear clutch slipping, oil passage leakage, transmission one-way clutch.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), linkage (2), idling rpm (3), air check (4), rear lubrication (5), band servo (6), low & reverse brake (7), front clutch (8), rear clutch (9), oil passage leakage (10), transmission one-way clutch (11).

symptom: Vehicle will not run in any range.
probable_cause: Low oil level, range select linkage, engine idling rpm, air check, rear lubrication, band servo, low and reverse brake, oil pump, or torque converter one-way clutch.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), linkage (2), engine idling rpm (3), air check (4), rear lubrication (5), band servo (6), low and reverse brake (7), oil pump (8), torque converter one-way clutch (9).

probable_cause: Range select linkage misadjusted, transmission air check failure, rear lubrication issue, or seized rear clutch.
corrective_action: Check range select linkage (1), air check (2), rear lubrication (3), rear clutch (4).

symptom: Maximum speed not attained. Acceleration poor.
probable_cause: Low oil level, linkage, air check, idling rpm, throttle oil pressure, governor valve, rear lubrication, engine adjustment/brakes, band brake, low & reverse brake, rear clutch, front clutch, oil pump.
corrective_action: Perform checks in sequence: oil level (1), linkage (2), air check (3), idling rpm (4), throttle pressure (5), governor (6), rear lubrication (7), brakes (8), band brake (9), low/rev brake (10), rear clutch (11), front clutch (12), oil pump (13).

symptom: Failure to change gear from '2nd' to '3rd'.
probable_cause: Range select linkage, vacuum diaphragm/piping, kickdown switch/solenoid, air check, rear lubrication, manual control valve, band servo, governor valve, band brake, oil passage leakage.
corrective_action: Check linkage (1), vacuum diaphragm (2), kickdown solenoid (3), air check (4), rear lubrication (5), manual valve (6), band servo (7), governor valve (8), band brake (9), oil passage leakage (10).

symptom: Failure to change gear from '1st' to '2nd'.
probable_cause: Linkage, vacuum diaphragm, downshift solenoid, air check, rear lubrication, manual valve, band servo, governor valve, band brake, oil passage leakage, front clutch check ball.
corrective_action: Follow inspection sequence: linkage (1), vacuum diaphragm (2), downshift solenoid (3), air check (4), rear lubrication (5), manual valve (6), band servo (7), governor valve (8), band brake (9), oil passage leakage (10), front clutch check ball (11).

symptom: Too high a gear change point from '1st' to '2nd', from '2nd' to '3rd'.
probable_cause: Vacuum diaphragm and piping, downshift solenoid/kickdown switch, throttle oil pressure, air check, rear lubrication, manual control valve, oil passage leakage.
corrective_action: Check vacuum diaphragm/piping (1), kickdown switch/solenoid (2), throttle pressure (3), air check (4), rear lubrication (5), manual valve (6), oil passage leakage (7).

probable_cause: Incorrect oil level, rear lubrication failure, throttle oil pressure, engine stall rpm, oil quantity, manual control valve, air check, band servo, clutches/brakes slipping, planetary gear binding.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), rear lubrication (2), throttle pressure (3), stall rpm (4), oil quantity (5), manual valve (6), air check (7), band servo (8), clutches/brakes (9-14), planetary gear (15).

symptom: Oil shoots out during operation. White smoke emitted from exhaust pipe during operation.
probable_cause: Punctured vacuum diaphragm absorbing ATF into engine intake, excessive oil level, or restricted oil cooler circuits.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), rear lubrication (2), vacuum diaphragm and piping (3), oil quantity (4), throttle pressure (5), stall rpm (6), manual valve (7), air check (8), clutches/brakes (9-14), planetary gear (15).

symptom: Offensive smell at oil charging pipe.
probable_cause: Burnt clutch facings or brake band friction linings due to severe slippage or low fluid level.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), air check (2), inspect rear clutch (3), front clutch (4), band brake (5), low & reverse brake (6), oil pump (7), oil passages (8), torque converter one-way clutch (9), planetary gear (10).

probable_cause: Oil level low, incorrect engine idling rpm, or defective oil pump.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), engine idling rpm (2), oil pump (3).

probable_cause: Oil level, engine idling rpm, rear clutch, oil pump, torque converter one-way clutch, front clutch check ball.
corrective_action: Check oil level (1), idling rpm (2), rear clutch (3), oil pump (4), torque converter one-way clutch (5), front clutch check ball (6).

symptom: Blown fuse or melted fusible link
probable_cause: Short circuit in power supply or heavy load-carrying circuit
corrective_action: Systematically trace circuit for shorts or grounding before installing new fuse. Never use higher rating fuse or wrap fusible links in vinyl tape.

symptom: Poor electrical contact or excessive circuit voltage drop
probable_cause: Rust, corrosion, or dirt on fuse clips or terminal blades
corrective_action: Clean metal contact surfaces with fine-grained sandpaper until shiny bare metal contact is made.

symptom: Glove box lamp stays ON or fails to illuminate
corrective_action: Inspect continuity: when plunger is pressed in, continuity must not exist; when plunger projects out, continuity must exist.

symptom: Combination switch failure (lights, wipers, or turn signals inoperative)
probable_cause: Internal contact wear or loose connector terminal
corrective_action: Check continuity across designated connector terminal pairs per Fig. BE-41 matrix; check alignment of tab in steering column jacket.

symptom: Headlamps do not light for either high or low beams.
Headlamps do not light for either high or low beams.
Headlamps do not light for either high or low beams.
corrective_action: Conduct continuity test and replace if necessary.

Both water temperature and oil pressure gauges do not operate.
corrective_action: Check for operation of circuits (i.e., fuel gauge and turn signal lamp) electrically connected to ignition relay. If they do not function, replace ignition relay.

Both water temperature and oil pressure gauges indicate inaccurately.

symptom: Both water temperature and oil pressure gauges indicate inaccurately.

probable_cause: Faulty thermal transmitter or loose terminal connection. (When thermal transmitter yellow/white wire is grounded, gauge pointer fluctuates.)
corrective_action: Replace thermal transmitter or correct terminal connection.

Water temperature gauge does not operate.

Faulty water temperature gauge. (Gauge pointer indicates maximum temperature even after ignition switch is turned off.)

corrective_action: [Connect a 116Ω resistance between thermal transmitter yellow/white wire and ground. When gauge indicates approximately 50°C (122°F), gauge is serviceable].

symptom: Water temperature gauge does not operate accurately.

corrective_action: Replace oil pressure sending unit or correct terminal connection.

Faulty oil pressure gauge. (Gauge pointer indicates maximum pressure even after ignition switch is turned off.)

corrective_action: Check for operation of circuits (i.e., water temperature, oil pressure gauge and turn signal lamp) electrically connected to ignition relay. If they do not function, replace ignition relay.

corrective_action: Replace tank unit or correct terminal connection.

symptom: Windshield wiper does not operate (Power supply and cable)
probable_cause: Blown fuse due to problem in other part of windshield wiper circuit
corrective_action: Check other part for operation and correct problem.

symptom: Windshield wiper does not operate (Power supply and cable)
corrective_action: Check wiring near motor and connector for proper connection. Correct if necessary.

symptom: Windshield wiper does not operate (Power supply and cable)
corrective_action: Check each wire for color code, and correct if necessary.

symptom: Windshield wiper does not operate (Power supply and cable)

symptom: Windshield wiper does not operate (Windshield wiper blade)
probable_cause: Windshield wiper blade sticks on windshield glass
corrective_action: Raise arm and operate windshield wiper without applying load. Clean windshield glass and/or replace wiper blade.

symptom: Windshield wiper speed cannot be adjusted correctly (Motor)
probable_cause: Low or high speed motor brush is worn

symptom: Windshield wiper does not stop correctly - Stops anywhere (Motor)
probable_cause: Contaminated auto-stop relay contacts or improper contact due to foreign matter
corrective_action: Remove auto-stop device cover, and clean contacts carefully so as not to deform relay plate.

symptom: Windshield wiper does not stop correctly - Stops anywhere (Cable and switch)
probable_cause: Improper connection between 1st and 2nd switch steps
corrective_action: Remove switch, and make sure that 1st and 2nd steps are not connected at 'OFF' position. If connected, replace switch.

symptom: Windshield wiper does not stop correctly - Does not stop (Motor)
probable_cause: Incomplete auto-stop operation (Contact is not interrupted.)
corrective_action: Remove auto-stop device cover, and correct relay plate bending.

symptom: Windshield wiper operating speed is too slow (Motor)
probable_cause: With arm raised, excessive current still flows due to layer short-circuit of motor armature

symptom: Windshield wiper operating speed is too slow (Motor)

symptom: Windshield wiper operating speed is too slow (Motor)
probable_cause: With arm raised, excessive current still flows (3 to 5A) due to seized motor shaft
corrective_action: Replace motor or lubricate bearing with engine oil.

symptom: Windshield wiper operating speed is too slow (Power supply and cable)
corrective_action: Measure voltage, check other electrical parts for operation, and take corrective action for power supply if necessary.

symptom: Windshield wiper operating speed is too slow (Link)
probable_cause: Humming occurs on motor in arm operating cycle due to seized arm shaft

symptom: Windshield wiper operating speed is too slow (Switch)
corrective_action: Conduct continuity test, and replace if necessary.

symptom: Ignition system: Noise occurs when engine is operated
corrective_action: Install new high tension cable. Replace a 0.5µF radio condenser of primary side + terminal of ignition coil. (Note: Be careful not to install capacitor to secondary or primary breaker side, otherwise engine operation becomes improper.)

symptom: Charging system: Sound of alternating current present; When accelerator pedal is depressed or released, noise occurs
corrective_action: Replace a 0.5µF capacitor to charging terminal B or charge warning terminal L. (Note: Do not use a larger capacitor.)

symptom: Fuel system: When ignition switch is set to 'ON', noise occurs
corrective_action: Install a 0.5µF capacitor to power lead connector plug of electric fuel pump.

symptom: Floor temperature warning lamp does not light in 'START' position of ignition switch
corrective_action: Replace bulb or correct bulb socket.

symptom: Floor temperature warning lamp does not light in 'START' position of ignition switch
corrective_action: Conduct continuity test and repair or replace. Refer to 'EC' section.

symptom: Floor temperature warning lamp does not light in 'START' position of ignition switch
corrective_action: Check wiring and/or repair if necessary.

symptom: Bumper shock absorber fails to return to original position after compression test
probable_cause: Internal binding, mechanical damage, or loss of high-pressure gas charge

symptom: Door window regulator handle operating force exceeds 3.5 kg (7.7 lb)
probable_cause: Insufficient lubrication, incorrect glass-to-panel clearance, or misaligned/non-parallel guide rails
corrective_action: (1) Lubricate guide rollers, guide rails and regulator linkage; (2) Perform weatherstrip-to-door glass adjustment; (3) Adjust guide rails in parallel

symptom: Door window glass tilts forward or rearward in door sash
corrective_action: Adjust guide channel A up if front tilts down (condition A), or down if rear tilts down (condition B)

symptom: Seat belt buckle switch fails inspection (test light does not go out when latched or go on when unlatched)
probable_cause: Worn, deformed, or faulty switch contacts or internal push rod mechanism
Swollen master cylinder seals due to poor fluid quality or contamination by kerosene, gasoline or mineral oil.
corrective_action: Flush the system, replace all rubber parts, refill with new fluid and air bleed the lines.

probable_cause: Pistons or valve carrier locked by deposits of fluid, foreign matter, etc.
Seized master cylinder piston due to infiltrations of water through rear end due to faulty boot or seals.

symptom: Engine cranks vigorously but will not fire or start; catches momentarily only when ignition key is released from START to ON
probable_cause: Open circuit in ballast bypass circuit: Black/Red (BR) wire from starter solenoid terminal 'R' to ignition coil (+) post is broken, disconnected, or starter solenoid internal auxiliary contact is oxidized.
corrective_action: Check continuity on Black/Red wire between starter terminal R and ignition coil (+) terminal. Inspect starter solenoid auxiliary terminal; verify 12V is present at coil (+) during key crank.

symptom: Fuel pump does not run during engine cranking or running
probable_cause: Faulty Air Flow Meter fuel pump interlock switch (pins 34-35), defective Fuel Pump Relay, blown 20A fuse, or corroded rear fuel pump ground eyelet.
corrective_action: Check continuity between AFM terminals 34 and 35 when flap is manually deflected. Check for 12V at Green wire at fuel pump connector C-2 during cranking. Clean dedicated fuel pump ground connection in rear spare tire well.

symptom: Engine starts cold and dies immediately; extreme hesitation and black exhaust smoke upon acceleration
probable_cause: Defective Water Temperature Sensor or open circuit in harness wires Red/Yellow (RY) or Black (B) to ECU pins 13 and 16, causing computer to assume coolant temperature is -40°C.
corrective_action: Measure resistance across ECU pins 13 and 16 at the 35-pin connector. Normal cold reading at 20°C is ~2.5 kΩ, dropping to ~300Ω at normal operating temperature. Replace sensor if open circuit.

symptom: Brake warning light in combination meter remains illuminated continuously with handbrake fully released
probable_cause: Master cylinder brake fluid level is low, fluid level float switch stuck down, parking brake lever switch bent/shorted to ground, or Warning Lamp Check Relay stuck closed.
corrective_action: Inspect brake fluid levels in front and rear master cylinder reservoirs. Disconnect fluid level switch harness; if light extinguishes, top off fluid or replace reservoir cap float assembly. Inspect handbrake switch contact.

symptom: Intermittent windshield wipers inoperative, but Low and High speeds function normally
probable_cause: Faulty Intermittent Wiper Amplifier on relay bracket, defective wiper switch INT contact (Blue/Red wire), or missing ground connection on amplifier Black lead.
corrective_action: Check for switched 12V on Blue wire at Intermittent Wiper Amplifier. Verify ground on Black wire. Check continuity of Blue/Red wire between steering column wiper switch and amplifier.

symptom: Battery discharges overnight or undercharges; red CHARGE indicator lamp does not illuminate with key ON before starting
probable_cause: Burnt-out charge warning bulb in speedometer, blown meter fuse (Fuse 6, 10A), or disconnected Yellow/White wire at IC regulator terminal 'L'. (Excitation current through bulb is required to initialize alternator charging field).
corrective_action: Replace defective charge warning bulb in combination meter. Verify 12V on Black/White wire to IC regulator terminal IG and inspect Yellow/White wire continuity between meter and regulator.

symptom: Starter motor does not crank (no click, no turnover)
probable_cause: Battery discharged; loose battery terminals; blown brown fusible link; faulty ignition switch STA contact; faulty inhibitor switch (A/T) out of adjustment; open starter solenoid
corrective_action: Check battery voltage (min 12.4V); clean battery terminals; inspect brown fusible link; bypass inhibitor switch to verify; check for 12V on BY wire at Starter S terminal during cranking

symptom: Engine cranks vigorously but will not start (no spark)
probable_cause: Blown Fuse 10; faulty ignition relay; failed transistor ignition unit; open ignition coil primary/secondary windings; disconnected distributor pickup coil shielded leads
corrective_action: Verify 12V on BW wire at Ignition Coil (+) with key ON; test primary (0.84–1.02Ω) and secondary (8.2–12.4kΩ) coil resistance; verify trigger pulse on blue wire from transistor ignition unit
page_label: Zone 1: Front/Left — Headlights, Alternator, Starter & Ignition

symptom: Engine starts and runs for 2 seconds, then immediately dies
probable_cause: Air Flow Meter safety contacts not closing; disconnected AFM connector; faulty fuel pump control relay; vacuum leak between AFM and throttle body preventing flap movement
corrective_action: Inspect intake boot for splits; verify fuel pump runs during cranking via bypass; verify fuel pump relay stays energized when AFM flap is manually deflected open with key ON
page_label: Zone 2: Engine Compartment, Relays, Fusible Links & EFI System

symptom: Fuel pump does not run during cranking
probable_cause: Blown green EFI fusible link; faulty fuel pump control relay cranking coil; open fuel pump relay; faulty electric fuel pump motor or broken ground strap at rear chassis
corrective_action: Verify 12V at green EFI fusible link; check for 12V on BY wire at fuel pump control relay during crank; check for 12V and ground at fuel pump terminals near fuel tank
page_label: Zone 2: Engine Compartment, Relays, Fusible Links & EFI System

symptom: Alternator charge warning light stays lit with engine running
probable_cause: Worn alternator carbon brushes; blown internal diode in IC regulator; loose alternator belt; open Y (Sense) wire at fusible link; blown 10A Fuse 10
corrective_action: Check alternator belt tension; measure charging voltage across battery posts (13.8–14.8V @ 2000 RPM); inspect Y wire continuity to fusible link; test WB wire voltage at check connector
page_label: Zone 1: Front/Left — Headlights, Alternator, Starter & Ignition

symptom: All instrument gauges (Fuel, Temp) read abnormally high or peg maximum
probable_cause: Missing or loose instrument panel ground; poor chassis bonding behind center console
corrective_action: Check black ground wires behind center console gauge cluster; clean ground eyelet attachment to dashboard steel structure
page_label: Zone 3: Center Dash, Switches, Combination Meter & Steering Column

symptom: Turn signals inoperative or stay solid ON without flashing
probable_cause: Blown Fuse 9 (10A); burned out exterior bulb (insufficient current draw to cycle thermal flasher); faulty 3-pin turn signal flasher unit; dirty combination switch contacts
corrective_action: Inspect Fuse 9; check all exterior turn bulbs (27W); replace 3-pin flasher unit; clean turn switch stalk contacts with electrical contact cleaner
page_label: Zone 3: Center Dash, Switches, Combination Meter & Steering Column

symptom: Windshield wipers do not park (stop immediately when switched OFF)
probable_cause: Dirty or worn auto-park contact switch inside wiper motor gearbox; faulty intermittent wiper amplifier module; open P terminal circuit
corrective_action: Check continuity between P and B terminals on wiper motor; clean internal park cam contacts; inspect ground lead on wiper amplifier module
page_label: Zone 2: Engine Compartment, Relays, Fusible Links & EFI System

symptom: Heater blower motor operates only on HIGH speed
probable_cause: Thermal fuse blown or open resistor coil in heater resistor pack; corroded resistor connector
corrective_action: Remove heater resistor pack from blower discharge duct; check continuity across each stepped resistor section; replace resistor assembly if any coil is open
page_label: Zone 4: Cabin, Fuse Box Circuits, HVAC, Audio & Center Console

symptom: Rear combination lamps dim, flicker, or cross-illuminate when turn signals flash
probable_cause: Corroded common ground eyelet in rear tail light pocket; poor body earth contact

symptom: Difficult fuel pump priming after running out of fuel

symptom: Cylinder misfire, rough running, or erratic injection
probable_cause: Contaminants lodged in precision injector nozzle or internal screen due to depleted filter
corrective_action: Replace high-pressure fuel filter (normal service interval 25,000 miles)

symptom: Erratic idle speed, rough idle, or improper air-fuel mixture ratio
probable_cause: Vacuum leak between air flow meter and intake valves allowing unmetered air to bypass flap
corrective_action: Inspect and seal all rubber intake ducts, throttle body gaskets, auxiliary air hoses, and manifold joints

symptom: Engine flooding during extended cold cranking
probable_cause: Cold start valve remaining open or defective thermotime switch failing to open internal contacts
corrective_action: Check thermotime switch bimetal heater and contacts (must open and interrupt cold start valve ground within 12 seconds)

probable_cause: Ignition system fault; manifold vacuum leaks; fuel pump/pressure regulator inoperative; missing ignition trigger input to ECU; faulty power relay or ECU
corrective_action: Check hot spark from coil; inspect PCV, dipstick, oil cap, AFM hoses for leaks; check fuel pump operation and regulator buzzing in START position; test ignition lead wire for 12V; test injector clicking every 3rd pulse; perform circuit tests 1-(6), 1-(3a-3c), 3-(3), 1-(5), 3-(1), 3-(2); test power relay

symptom: Engine Hard To Start Only When Cold
probable_cause: Low battery cranking voltage (< 9.6V); cold start valve inoperative; cold start circuit 3-(3) wiring fault; defective thermotime switch
corrective_action: Check battery voltage while cranking (must be >= 9.6V); perform circuit check 3-(3); perform cold start valve component test (EF-54)

symptom: Engine Hard To Start Only When Hot (Above 170°F)
probable_cause: Cold start valve leaking or operating when engine hot (flooding); defective thermotime switch sticking closed; fuel vapor lock or improper fuel pressure; leaking injectors; water temp sensor fault
corrective_action: Disconnect cold start valve, clear flooded fuel, and crank; if engine starts easily, disconnect thermotime switch to isolate whether valve or switch is defective; perform circuit test 1-(6), 1-(3a-3c), fuel pressure test, and injector leakage test

probable_cause: Defective air flow meter fuel pump switch contacts; missing ignition signal input; power relay not holding in ON position; water temperature sensor circuit fault; defective auxiliary air regulator
corrective_action: Verify ignition lead wire has 12V in ON; listen for injector clicking; check power relay clicks twice (ON and START); push open AFM flap with ignition ON to test fuel pump run; perform circuit test 1-(6) and check auxiliary air regulator

symptom: Engine Idles Too Fast — Cannot Be Adjusted With Speed Screw Or Engine Idle Is Unstable
probable_cause: Auxiliary air regulator stuck open or heater circuit open; throttle plate not closing fully; sticking EGR valve; B.C.D.D. valve open at idle; manifold vacuum leaks (PCV, dipstick, oil cap, AFM boots); throttle valve switch out of adjustment
corrective_action: Pinch off auxiliary air regulator hose with pliers: if idle drops, test circuit 1-(8) or replace regulator; check throttle plate stop; check EGR valve seating; check BCDD relief solenoid; check intake for false air leaks; perform circuit tests 1-(1) through 1-(8)

symptom: Engine Misfires — HC Reading Too High
probable_cause: Ignition system defect; voltage regulator over/under-charging; loose or corroded harness connectors; clogged fuel filter or tank strainer; leaking/dirty injectors; faulty ECU internal connection
corrective_action: Check ignition thoroughly; check charging system voltage; disconnect, inspect, and clean all EFI connectors; check fuel supply circuit for blockage; tap ECU while driving to check for intermittent internal fault; check fuel pressure (EF-57); perform circuit tests

symptom: Engine Will Not Rev. — Lack Of Power
probable_cause: Transistor ignition pickup coil or coil failure; throttle plate not opening fully; AFM flap sticking or binding mechanically; fuel filter or tank strainer restricted; low fuel pressure; full throttle switch or AFM circuit faults
corrective_action: Check transistor ignition pickup coils; verify throttle linkage reaches full wide open; remove intake boot and verify AFM flap opens fully and smoothly by hand; check fuel filter/lines; perform fuel pressure test; perform circuit tests 1-(2), 2-(1), 2-(2), 2-(3a-3f), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(1), 1-(4), 1-(6), 1-(8)

probable_cause: Air flow meter flap sticking or encountering mechanical resistance; unmetered intake air/vacuum leaks; low fuel pressure; throttle switch transition fault
corrective_action: Remove intake hose from AFM and check flap movement with finger; replace AFM if any resistance or binding is felt; check intake manifold and PCV hoses for leaks; check fuel pressure; perform complete circuit tests

symptom: Poor Gas Mileage, Or CO Reading Too High
probable_cause: Incorrect ignition timing / weak spark; clogged air cleaner; excessive fuel pressure; defective water temperature sensor (enrichment on continuously); air temperature sensor fault; leaking cold start valve; dirty injectors
corrective_action: Check timing and spark energy; inspect air cleaner element; tee in pressure gauge at cold start valve to check fuel pressure; perform circuit tests 1-(6), 1-(4), 1-(1), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 3-(2), 1-(8), 2-(3a-3f)

probable_cause: Mechanical binding or uneven resistance in air flow meter flap; manifold vacuum leaks; intermittent throttle switch or AFM resistor track wear
corrective_action: Check AFM flap for smoothness of operation; inspect PCV valve, dipstick seal, oil cap seal, and manifold gaskets; perform circuit tests 1-(1), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(5), 1-(9a-9d), 1-(4), 1-(6), 1-(8), 2-(1), 2-(2), 2-(3a-3f)

probable_cause: Intake manifold vacuum leaks; lean air-fuel mixture; defective idle/full throttle switch; water temp sensor open circuit; injector circuit fault
corrective_action: Check for manifold vacuum leaks (PCV, dipstick, oil cap, AFM hoses); perform circuit tests 1-(1), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(4), 1-(6), 2-(1), 2-(2), 2-(3a-3f)

probable_cause: Throttle valve switch misadjusted (idle contact not closing during deceleration); rich fuel mixture or leaking injector; ignition timing/spark defect; start signal circuit remaining energized
corrective_action: Perform circuit tests 1-(1) (idle switch), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(4), 1-(6), 2-(3a-3f), and 3-(1) ('Start' signal circuit); check throttle switch adjustment (EF-65)

corrective_action: Perform component checks per 1975 280Z Service Manual: Injector Sound (EF-57), Auxiliary Air Regulator (EF-58), Control Unit Replacement (EF-51), AFM Flap Operation (EF-51), AFM Resistance/Voltage Meas. (EF-52), Fuel Pressure Test (EF-56/7), Pressure Regulator (EF-57).

corrective_action: Perform component checks per 1975 280Z Service Manual: Injector Sound (EF-57), AFM Flap Operation (EF-51), AFM Resistance/Voltage Meas. (EF-52), Fuel Pressure Test (EF-56/7), Injector Leakage (EF-57), Cold Start Valve Leakage (EF-54), Pressure Regulator (EF-57).

symptom: Engine runs excessively rich (black exhaust smoke, carbon-fouled plugs, sooty tailpipe, exhaust backfiring, poor fuel economy)
probable_cause: AFM black wheel adjusted too loose (under-tensioned); measuring flap sticking open; leaking cold start valve; CHT/coolant temperature sensor disconnected or corroded; stuck thermotime switch; fuel pressure excessive; wiper shorted
corrective_action: Check and clean spark plugs; inspect CHT/water temp sensor harness for corrosion; test cold start valve; rotate AFM black wheel Clockwise (CW) in ~4-tooth increments to increase spring tension; verify flap pivots freely

symptom: Engine runs dangerously lean (intake backfire/'front fire', severe hesitation on acceleration, white spark plug insulators with melted electrode erosion, high engine temperatures)
probable_cause: AFM black wheel adjusted too tight (over-tensioned); unmetered vacuum leak (cracked intake boot, split vacuum hoses, valve cover or manifold gasket leak); fuel pressure too low; clogged injectors; idle bypass screw opened too far
corrective_action: Perform smoke/vacuum leak inspection; test fuel pump delivery pressure; perform live 'fingering' check (deflect wiper CCW to test enrichment); rotate black wheel Counter-Clockwise (CCW) in ~4-tooth increments to reduce tension; readjust idle bypass screw

symptom: Engine starts on cranking but stalls immediately when ignition key is released to ON
probable_cause: AFM fuel pump safety shut-off switch contacts dirty, oxidized, or out of adjustment (Pins 36 and 39 failing to make contact when flap opens); fuel switch actuator pin misaligned
corrective_action: Measure resistance across Pins 36 and 39 while deflecting flap (must drop from ∞ to 0 Ω immediately as flap opens); clean switch contacts with Caig DeoxIT; adjust silver actuator arm if required

symptom: Flat spot, stumble, or dead hesitation during throttle tip-in or mid-range acceleration
probable_cause: Potentiometer wiper arm resting off the clockwise end of the carbon track (registering open circuit at idle); carbon trace worn, scratched, or contaminated with oil/carbon film; wiper finger tension weak
corrective_action: Clean ceramic carbon trace and wiper fingers with DeoxIT; ensure wiper rests 2-4 mm before end of track when flap is closed; loosen center pivot locking screw to recalibrate wiper sweep if resting off track

symptom: Black wheel recoils violently ('sprong') and loses all spring preload
probable_cause: Locking screw loosened or removed without maintaining firm finger counter-pressure on the black toothed gear wheel
corrective_action: Re-engage clock spring; realign to previously scribed reference marks or factory glue residue (~2.5-3 teeth lean of power setting); perform live engine fingering test at idle and 3,000 RPM to recalibrate base tension

symptom: Measuring flap bent, binding, or destroyed after intake backfire ('front fire')
probable_cause: Idle air bypass screw was turned fully CW (bottomed out), sealing the secondary passage and eliminating the pressure relief corridor for intake backfire shock waves
corrective_action: Replace or carefully straighten measuring flap; verify flap swings without rubbing or binding throughout complete arc; back out idle air bypass screw to restore pressure relief corridor

symptom: False lean condition incorrectly compensated by over-enriching the AFM
probable_cause: Over-advanced ignition timing; unmetered air leaks in intake boots, PCV, or valve cover gasket bypassing the AFM flap
corrective_action: Check and set base ignition timing to factory specification on under-hood label; repair all vacuum and intake duct leaks before modifying AFM spring tension
